anarchist

/AN-er-kist/ - the stress falls on AN · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Anarchist means one who wants to eliminate all government.

The old dockhand was an anarchist of the quiet kind, certain that people could run their own affairs with no state above them.

Example

At the history fair, Priya's display profiled a 1930s anarchist newspaper whose editors wanted no government whatsoever — not fairer taxes or kinder courts, but no taxes and no courts, with bakeries and bridges alike run by the people who used them.

Anarchist is a precise label, not a loose insult: it names someone who would eliminate all government. A person who merely breaks rules is unruly; a person who wants lighter rules is a reformer; only the person who wants no rulers at all is an anarchist.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

rebel: A rebel fights the particular authority over them and may happily crown a new one once it falls. An anarchist opposes rulers as such: not this king or that law, but the existence of government itself. Every anarchist is against the regime; most rebels only want a different one.

nihilist: A nihilist rejects all values and meaning — morality, truth, purpose — not just the state. An anarchist's target is narrower and political: government must go, but community, cooperation, and ethics can stay. An anarchist may believe deeply in human goodness; a nihilist believes in nothing.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

statist: looks first to government to organize and solve

loyalist: stands by the established regime, come what may

Where it sits · how much of government must go

dissenter → revolutionary → anarchist

dissenter vs. anarchist: A dissenter is far milder than an anarchist — objecting to this policy or that ruler while leaving government itself standing.

revolutionary vs. anarchist: A revolutionary stops short of the anarchist: revolutionaries topple a government to build another, while the anarchist would leave the ground bare.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — an-: without

Root — arch: ruler (Greek archos)

Suffix — -ist: one who believes or practices

Put it together: An- (without) + arch- (ruler) + -ist (one who believes) = one who believes in no ruler. Greek arkhos is the ruler at the head of things; the anarchist's whole program is packed into the prefix — take the ruler away.

Use the root in a new word: monarch: The portrait gallery devotes an entire wing to monarchs no one can now name.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / political

Anarchist is a precise political label, not a synonym for troublemaker: it names someone who would eliminate government itself. A rule-breaker is unruly; a protester wants better rules. And keep it apart from libertarian (this unit), who would shrink the state, not erase it.
